# **Gaps — no SOP yet**

• **Member Onboarding** — no standardised first-touch-to-first-class pathway; inconsistent induction, goal-setting, intro offer mechanics, and safety screening
• **Cancellation & Churn** — no documented exit interview, win-back trigger, or reason capture; revenue leakage invisible

• **Weekly Key Coach Tasks** — no clarity on what coaches own beyond class delivery (member follow-ups, feedback, admin, cleaning); accountability gaps
• **Member Data Privacy & GDPR** — critical gap for a women's-only gym; consent, data retention, subject access requests uncontrolled
• **Order Supplies & Sundries** — likely ad-hoc; no reorder points, vendor list, or budget ownership
• **Referral Programme** — no mechanics, tracking, or incentive SOP; leaving word-of-mouth unstructured

# Concrete Execution for Service Menu Creation

• **Start with your revenue reality, not your dreams.** Pull your last 3 months of actual sales data. What are people *actually* buying? Build your menu around those top 5-6 revenue drivers first, then add 1-2 aspirational offerings. This prevents menu paralysis and ensures coaches know what to sell.

• **Create TWO separate, brutally honest menus.** Coach version = margin, upsell triggers, and what's included in each tier so they stop giving away premium services. Member version = benefits-focused language with price anchoring (put the priciest option first so mid-tier looks reasonable).

• **Price by session/package, not hourly rates.** Instead of "£45/hour PT," offer "8-week Body Composition Program £320" (£40/session). Packages commit members, improve retention, and feel like value. Include what's *not* included (e.g., "does not include nutrition coaching") to kill scope creep.

• **Get coach input in a structured 30-minute call, not a group chat.** Ask: "What service do you wish members understood better?" and "What do you overdeliver on that we should charge for?" Their frontline feedback prevents a menu that doesn't sell.

• **Post internally and test pricing for one week before going public.** Get real objections from your members. You'll catch pricing gaps and confusing bundling before it hits your reputation.
